proof: The benchmark pairs every treatment trial with a baseline trial of the same task and repeat, and reports for input tokens: the pairs, both medians, the mean and median of the paired deltas, a deterministic bootstrap 95% interval and the share of the baseline the delta represents. An unpaired trial contributes nothing and is named. Input tokens are the provider's own count, recorded on the log as ModelUsageRecorded and read back through the task economics view. Three paired trials of one task through the real Core, measured from the canonical log. Each variant does what an agent can do with the machinery it has: the treatment asks for a Context Pack and runs with compaction, the baseline reads the files it needs with compaction effectively off. The model, the task, the repository and the machine are held constant, and the report names what varied. On this run the machinery cut the prompt by 54% (13809 to 6386 input tokens) and the tool calls from 4 to 1, with the same verified outcome in both variants.
audit: NOT-FOUND before this task: nothing compared two configurations of the product on the same work.
limitations: The model is a deterministic local server, so the paired trials are identical and the bootstrap interval has no width: the report says so rather than implying variance a real provider would have. The variants differ by what each script does with the tools it has, which measures the machinery under its intended use rather than a model's spontaneous behaviour; whether a model left to itself would reach for retrieval, and how many calls it would make, is REQ-EV-0251 and REQ-EV-0253 and needs a live provider.
